title: Robot not connecting on the field
summary: Driver station to FMS, radio link, roboRIO link. Work left to right on the field monitor.

start.question: Look at the field monitor, left to right. What is the first thing that is not green?
start.help: The DS reports every status. The radio cannot show linked until the DS is linked, and the RIO cannot show linked until the radio is.

options.label: All green but the robot drops or lags in matches

ds-ethernet.question: On the DS laptop, open the Diagnostics tab. Is Enet Link lit?
ds-ethernet.help: Enet Link means the laptop sees something on its Ethernet port. If it is off, nothing else matters yet.

options.label: Yes, but FMS is still red

ds-no-ethernet.title: DS laptop has no Ethernet link
steps: Unplug the field cable from the laptop and plug it back in until it clicks. Check the other end at the player station.
Reseat the USB Ethernet adapter if the laptop uses one. Try a different USB port.
Run ncpa.cpl. Make sure the Ethernet adapter is enabled, not greyed out.
Replace the field Ethernet cable with a spare.

steps.text: Does the port still show no link?

steps: Try a different port on the SCC at the player station. One of the AUX ports should work.

steps.text: Still no link on the AUX port?
steps.yes: Use a USB Ethernet adapter or a loaner laptop.

ds-team-number.question: Open the DS Setup tab. Does the team number match the team in this match?

ds-wrong-team.title: Fix the team number in the DS
steps: Type the correct team number in the Setup tab and press Enter. Click outside the box so it takes effect.
A shared laptop between two teams needs the number checked every match.

steps.text: Is the FMS light still red after 10 seconds?
steps.yes: Work the 'DS has link but no FMS' steps in this guide.

ds-no-fms.title: DS has link but no FMS
steps: Make sure the FRC Driver Station software is open, and only one copy. Close any extra and reopen it.
Turn Wi-Fi off with the hardware switch or Quick Settings.
Restart the Driver Station software.
Open the Diagnostics tab and check Firewall. If Dom, Pub, or Prv are orange, run wf.msc and disable the firewall on all three profiles: Domain, Private, and Public.
In ncpa.cpl, disable every network adapter except the field Ethernet.
Set the Ethernet adapter to a static IP of 10.TE.AM.200, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, and leave the gateway and DNS servers blank.
Check for and disable any third-party firewall or antivirus.
Try a different Ethernet NIC, such as a USB Ethernet dongle.

steps.text: Is the DS still red with no FMS?

radio-lights.question: Look at the radio on the robot. What do the lights show?
radio-lights.help: VH-109 lights, left to right: PWR, SYS, 2.4G, 6G, RIO.

options.label: PWR on, SYS blinking about once a second

radio-no-power.title: Radio has no power
steps: Confirm the robot is on. Check the roboRIO Power light is green.
Find the PDH or PDP channel that feeds the radio. Check the fuse or breaker is seated and the channel LED is not red.
PoE power only works on the radio's RIO port. If PoE is the source, make sure it is in the RIO port, not AUX1, AUX2, or DS.

If PoE: check the injector orientation. On the orange REV injector the male end plugs into the radio. On the black Vivid injector the female end takes the PoE, with a cable from there to the radio's RIO port.
If the DC input is the source: measure for battery voltage at the end of the power wires with a multimeter. No voltage means the wiring, not the radio.
Reseat the radio power connector, the Weidmuller DC plug or the PoE cable in the RIO port.
Remove one power source if PoE and the DC input are both wired. Use one only.

steps.text: Is the radio still dark with known good power?
steps.yes: Swap in a spare radio and program it at the kiosk.

radio-not-linked.title: Radio is up but cannot reach the field
steps: Wait 60 seconds after power on. The radio takes that long to boot and join the field.
Reprogram the radio at this event's kiosk. A radio from another event or home has the wrong key.
Check for a second radio programmed for this event left powered on, often a spare at the pit. It associates with the field and confuses the connection.
The radio links to the field AP on its own and its status lights show that. The field monitor shows a partial connection until the DS is fully connected, then it goes green.

steps.text: Is SYS still blinking after a reprogram?

radio-ap-mode.title: Radio is in access point mode on battery
steps: All lights blinking fast means the radio is set to Access Point mode and sees battery power. Wireless is off in this state.
Take the radio to the kiosk and reprogram it in Robot Radio mode for this event.
Check the other radio is not the AP unit by mistake if the team has two.

steps.text: Do all lights still blink fast after a reprogram?

radio-linked-monitor-red.title: Radio pings the field but the monitor shows it red
steps: SYS solid means the radio can ping the field. The monitor turns green only after the DS is fully connected.
Go back to the DS. Confirm Enet Link, team number, and FMS green.
Wait 20 seconds after the DS turns green. The radio column follows.

steps.text: Is the radio still red with the DS green?

rio-lights.question: Look at the roboRIO. What are the Power and Status lights doing?

rio-power.title: roboRIO power problem
steps: Off: check the RIO power Weidmuller plug and the PDH or PDP RIO channel fuse. Tug test the wires.
Amber: brownout. Check battery voltage in the DS. Swap to a fully charged battery.
Red: short on a user rail. Unplug everything from the RIO power rails and DIO, then power cycle.
Check the main breaker lug nuts and battery connector are tight. Loose main power causes both amber and off.

steps.text: Is the Power light still red with nothing plugged in?

no-code.title: Everything green but No Code
steps: In the DS, click Restart Robot Code. Wait 15 seconds.
Ask if the code changed since it last worked. Check the DS Console for a stack trace or crash message.
Reboot the roboRIO from the DS or with the reset button. Wait for the Status light to turn off.
Redeploy if the code was built with a different WPILib year than the RIO image. A mismatch never runs.

steps.text: Does the DS still show No Code?
steps.yes: Read the crash in the DS Console with the team.

drops.title: Robot loses connection during matches
steps: Check for loose power or Ethernet wires at the radio. Reseat them. A loose connection drops the link under vibration.

Check the DS log battery voltage. The radio runs down to about 4.5 V, so a brownout rarely resets it. The roboRIO browns out and disables outputs first: 6.3 V on the roboRIO 1, 6.75 V by default on the roboRIO 2 (roboRIO 2 is configurable).
Remove one power source if the radio has both PoE and the DC input. Dual power causes reboots.

steps.text: Does the robot still drop in matches?

steps: Check the radio signal strength during the match: bars on the field monitor (FMS or FTA Buddy), or dB in the FMS station log.

steps.no: Keep working this robot's power and wiring.

steps: Low signal is the radio or the RF path. Use the lag branch of this guide for signal and the RF environment.

options.label: Robot loses connection or cuts out
Robot stays connected but is laggy or slow to respond

lag-check.question: Check the radio signal strength and trip time during the match (bars on the field monitor or FTA Buddy, dB in the FMS station log). What do you see?

options.label: Low signal or high trip time
Signal and trip time look normal

rf-environment.title: Low signal or high trip time: the RF path
steps: The link, not the robot, is the problem. Check the radio is at the top of the robot, in the open, away from motors and metal.
View the match logs in the FTA Buddy app if the extension is set up on the field. Check whether other robots in the match also had low signal or dropped packets.

steps.text: Did the whole field see it?
steps.yes: It is the field or RF environment, not this robot.

steps: Scan the 6 GHz spectrum near the field for rogue access points crowding the channel.
Rule out outside interference. A nearby airport's radar or an aircraft on approach has disrupted a field before. Watch whether the drops repeat with an outside event.

code-lag.title: Link is fine but the robot lags
steps: The radio link is fine, so the lag is in the robot or its code.
View the Driver Station log for roboRIO CPU usage and console messages about loop overruns.

steps.text: Is CPU high or are there loop overrun messages?
steps.yes: Fix the robot code. Use the Code and deploy guide, CPU branch.

steps: Look at the specific mechanism that lags: its sensors, its command, and any blocking calls in the code.

rio-eth-link.question: Look at the roboRIO Ethernet port. Are the link lights flashing quickly?

rio-eth-good.title: roboRIO Ethernet link is good
steps: The link lights mean the cable and the radio are fine. The problem is above the physical link.
Set the team number on the roboRIO with the Imaging Tool if it is wrong or unset.
Redeploy the robot code.

steps.text: Does the DS reach the roboRIO now?
steps.no: Work the roboRIO guide, or the DS side with the Driver station guide.
